records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

es.L: Y habló {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Moisés, diciendo:
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés:
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés:

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} parla à Moïse, en disant :
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse :
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse :

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akanena na Musa, akisema,
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa,
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa,

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("parla", "poursuivit"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit", "a poursuivi"); speech keeps the tenses of speech
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé that of the plain Readable level.

source.text: דַּבֵּר֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְיָשֻׁ֗בוּ וְיַחֲנוּ֙ לִפְנֵי֙ פִּ֣י הַחִירֹ֔ת בֵּ֥ין מִגְדֹּ֖ל וּבֵ֣ין הַיָּ֑ם לִפְנֵי֙ בַּ֣עַל צְפֹ֔ן נִכְח֥וֹ תַחֲנ֖וּ עַל־הַיָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel, that they turn back and camp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and between the sea; before Baal-zephon, opposite it, you will camp by the sea.

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, that they turn back and camp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea; before Baal-zephon, opposite it, you will camp by the sea.
en.B: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to turn around and set up camp in front of Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. Make your camp beside the sea, across from Baal-zephon.
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to go back and camp near a place called Pi-hahiroth. It is between Migdol and the sea. Have them camp by the sea, across from Baal-zephon.

es.L: «Habla a los hijos de Israel que se vuelvan y acampen delante de Pi-hahirot, entre Migdol y el mar; delante de Baal-zefón, frente a él, {{plural_you:acamparán|acamparéis}} junto al mar.
es.B: «Di a los israelitas que den la vuelta y acampen frente a Pi-hahirot, entre Migdol y el mar. {{plural_you:Acampen|Acampad}} junto al mar, frente a Baal-zefón.
es.R: «Diles a los israelitas que regresen y acampen cerca de un lugar llamado Pi-hahirot. Está entre Migdol y el mar. Que acampen junto al mar, frente a Baal-zefón.

fr.L: « Parle aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël : qu’ils se détournent et qu’ils campent devant Pi-Hahiroth, entre Migdol et la mer ; devant Baal-Tsephôn, en face, vous camperez près de la mer.
fr.B: « Dis aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} de faire demi-tour et de camper devant Pi-Hahiroth, entre Migdol et la mer. Vous établirez votre camp au bord de la mer, en face de Baal-Tsephôn.
fr.R: « Dis aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} de revenir en arrière et de camper près d’un endroit appelé Pi-Hahiroth. Il se trouve entre Migdol et la mer. Qu’ils campent au bord de la mer, en face de Baal-Tsephôn.

sw.L: "Sema na wana wa Israeli, kwamba warudi nyuma wapige kambi mbele ya Pi-hahirothi, kati ya Migdoli na bahari; mbele ya Baal-sefoni, kuelekeana nao, mtapiga kambi kando ya bahari.
sw.B: "Waambie Waisraeli wageuke, wapige kambi mbele ya Pi-hahirothi, kati ya Migdoli na bahari. Pigeni kambi yenu kando ya bahari, mkabala na Baal-sefoni.
sw.R: "Waambie Waisraeli warudi nyuma, wapige kambi karibu na mahali panapoitwa Pi-hahirothi. Ni kati ya Migdoli na bahari. Wapige kambi kando ya bahari, mkabala na Baal-sefoni.

decisions.choice: Pi-hahiroth, Migdol, Baal-zephon: places near the sea whose sites are not known for certain
decisions.reason: These names marked Israel's camp beside the sea (verse 9; Numbers 33:7-8). "Migdol" means "tower" or "fort", and Baal-zephon carries the name of the god Baal. None of the three places can be located with certainty today, so the exact route and the place of the crossing cannot be fixed from these names.

decisions.choice: turn back: a change of direction that God orders on purpose
decisions.reason: Israel had camped at the edge of the wilderness (13:20). Turning back puts them where they look trapped between the wilderness and the sea, and verses 3-4 give God's reason: to draw Pharaoh out after them.

decisions.choice: Make your camp ... / Have them camp ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew changes from "they" to "you" (plural) in the last clause. Balanced keeps the direct command; Readable keeps it as part of what Moses is to tell the people.

source.text: וְאָמַ֤ר פַּרְעֹה֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְבֻכִ֥ים הֵ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ סָגַ֥ר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And will say Pharaoh of [the] sons of Israel, wandering in confusion [are] they in the land; has shut on them the wilderness.

en.L: And Pharaoh will say of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, 'They [are] wandering in confusion in the land; the wilderness has closed [the way] on them.'
en.B: Pharaoh will say about the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'They are lost and wandering about the country; the wilderness has trapped them.'
en.R: Pharaoh will tell himself, 'The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are lost. They are wandering around, and the desert has them trapped.'

es.L: Y el faraón dirá de los hijos de Israel: “Andan errantes y confundidos por la tierra; el desierto les ha cerrado [el paso]”.
es.B: El faraón dirá de los israelitas: “Andan perdidos, vagando por el país; el desierto los tiene atrapados”.
es.R: El faraón pensará: “Los israelitas están perdidos. Andan dando vueltas, y el desierto los tiene atrapados”.

fr.L: Et Pharaon dira des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël : “Ils errent, égarés dans le pays ; le désert a fermé [le passage] sur eux.”
fr.B: Pharaon dira des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : “Ils sont perdus, ils errent dans le pays ; le désert les a pris au piège.”
fr.R: Pharaon se dira : “Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} sont perdus. Ils tournent en rond, et le désert les tient prisonniers.”

sw.L: Naye Farao atasema juu ya wana wa Israeli, 'Wanatangatanga wamechanganyikiwa katika nchi; nyika imewafungia [njia].'
sw.B: Farao atasema kuhusu Waisraeli, 'Wamepotea, wanazunguka-zunguka nchini; nyika imewanasa.'
sw.R: Farao atajiambia, 'Waisraeli wamepotea. Wanazunguka huku na huko, na jangwa limewanasa.'

decisions.choice: wandering in confusion: lost, not knowing which way to go
decisions.reason: The verb describes people who are confused and at a loss (Joel 1:18 uses it of cattle with no pasture; Esther 3:15 of a city in dismay). Pharaoh will think Israel has lost its way.

decisions.choice: the wilderness has shut them in: they are trapped
decisions.reason: With the wilderness behind them and the sea in front, Israel would look boxed in, an easy target for an army.

decisions.choice: will tell himself
decisions.reason: "Say" here is what Pharaoh will say or think about Israel, not words spoken to them. Readable makes that plain.

source.text: וְחִזַּקְתִּ֣י אֶת־לֵב־פַּרְעֹה֮ וְרָדַ֣ף אַחֲרֵיהֶם֒ וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל־חֵיל֔וֹ וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make strong [the] heart of Pharaoh, and he will pursue after them, and I will get glory by Pharaoh and by all his army, and will know Egypt that I [am] Yahweh. And they did so.

en.L: And I will make the heart of Pharaoh strong, and he will pursue after them, and I will get glory over Pharaoh and over all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And they did so.
en.B: I will make Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he will chase after them. Then I will win glory at the expense of Pharaoh and all his forces, and the Egyptians will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." The Israelites did as they were told.
en.R: I will make Pharaoh stubborn, and he will chase after them. But I will defeat Pharaoh and his whole army, and that will bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glory. Then the Egyptians will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." So the Israelites did what they were told.

es.L: Y fortaleceré el corazón del faraón, y él los perseguirá, y obtendré gloria sobre el faraón y sobre todo su ejército, y sabrán los egipcios que yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}». Y así lo hicieron.
es.B: Endureceré el corazón del faraón, y saldrá tras ellos. Entonces obtendré gloria a costa del faraón y de todo su ejército, y los egipcios sabrán que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}». Los israelitas hicieron lo que se les había mandado.
es.R: Haré que el faraón se ponga terco, y él saldrá a perseguirlos. Pero yo derrotaré al faraón y a todo su ejército, y eso {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dará gloria. Entonces los egipcios sabrán que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}». Así que los israelitas hicieron lo que se les mandó.

fr.L: Et je rendrai fort le cœur de Pharaon, et il les poursuivra, et je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glorifierai aux dépens de Pharaon et de toute son armée, et les Égyptiens sauront que je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. » Et ils firent ainsi.
fr.B: Je rendrai obstiné le cœur de Pharaon, et il se lancera à leur poursuite. Alors je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} couvrirai de gloire aux dépens de Pharaon et de toutes ses troupes, et les Égyptiens sauront que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. » Les Israélites firent ce qu’on leur avait dit.
fr.R: Je rendrai Pharaon têtu, et il va les poursuivre. Mais je vais vaincre Pharaon et toute son armée, et cela {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} donnera de la gloire. Alors les Égyptiens sauront que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. » Les Israélites ont donc fait ce qu’on leur avait dit.

sw.L: Nami nitautia nguvu moyo wa Farao, naye atawafuatia, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitajipatia utukufu juu ya Farao na juu ya jeshi lake lote, nao Wamisri watajua ya kuwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}." Nao wakafanya hivyo.
sw.B: Nitaufanya moyo wa Farao kuwa mgumu, naye atawafuata. Kisha nitajipatia utukufu kupitia Farao na majeshi yake yote, na Wamisri watajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}." Waisraeli wakafanya kama walivyoagizwa.
sw.R: Nitamfanya Farao kuwa mkaidi, naye atawafuata. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitamshinda Farao na jeshi lake lote, na jambo hilo litaniletea utukufu. Ndipo Wamisri watajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}." Kwa hiyo Waisraeli walifanya kama walivyoambiwa.

decisions.choice: I will make Pharaoh's heart strong: God confirms Pharaoh in his resistance
decisions.reason: The verb means to make firm or strong, as in 4:21 and 11:10. See the note at 7:3.

decisions.choice: I will get glory: be honored, show my weight
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the root "heavy", the root of Pharaoh's "heavy" heart (7:14; 9:7). Pharaoh made his heart heavy against God; now God will be "heavy", that is honored and glorious, through Pharaoh's defeat. The same verb returns in verses 17-18, and the root again in verse 25.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians will know that I am Yahweh: the purpose of the plagues reaches its end
decisions.reason: God said in 7:5 that the Egyptians would know that he is Yahweh when he brought Israel out. Pharaoh had asked, "Who is Yahweh?" (5:2).

decisions.choice: The Israelites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "they did so"; Balanced and Readable name the Israelites.

decisions.choice: I will defeat Pharaoh ... and that will bring me glory
decisions.reason: Readable says how God will win glory over Pharaoh: by defeating him, as the rest of the chapter tells.

decisions.choice: "je me glorifierai aux dépens de Pharaon" (L); "je me couvrirai de gloire aux dépens de Pharaon" (B), here and in verses 17-18
alternatives: "je ferai éclater ma gloire sur Pharaon"
decisions.reason: French says "get glory over" most naturally with a reflexive verb and "aux dépens de" (at the expense of), as the English Balanced does. The reflexive pronoun is God's, so it takes the deity_pronoun span, which the English "I will get glory" has no word for.

source.text: וַיֻּגַּד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח הָעָ֑ם וַ֠יֵּהָפֵךְ לְבַ֨ב פַּרְעֹ֤ה וַעֲבָדָיו֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם וַיֹּֽאמרוּ֙ מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֔ינוּ כִּֽי־שִׁלַּ֥חְנוּ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעָבְדֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to [the] king of Egypt that had fled the people, and was turned [the] heart of Pharaoh and his servants toward the people, and they said, what [is] this we have done, that we have let go Israel from serving us?

en.L: And it was told to the king of Egypt that the people had fled, and the heart of Pharaoh and his servants was turned against the people, and they said, "What [is] this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?"
en.B: Word reached the king of Egypt that the people had run away, and Pharaoh and his officials turned against them. "Why did we do this?" they said. "We have let Israel go, and they will no longer serve us!"
en.R: Someone told the king of Egypt that the Israelites had run away. Then Pharaoh and his officials turned against them. They said, "Why did we do this? We let the Israelites go, and now we have lost our slaves!"

es.L: Y se le informó al rey de Egipto que el pueblo había huido, y el corazón del faraón y de sus siervos se volvió contra el pueblo, y dijeron: «¿Qué [es] esto que hemos hecho, que hemos dejado ir a Israel para que no nos sirva?».
es.B: Le llegó al rey de Egipto la noticia de que el pueblo había huido, y el faraón y sus funcionarios se volvieron contra ellos. «¿Por qué hicimos esto?», dijeron. «¡Hemos dejado ir a Israel, y ya no nos servirá!».
es.R: Alguien le contó al rey de Egipto que los israelitas habían escapado. Entonces el faraón y sus funcionarios se pusieron en contra de ellos. Dijeron: «¿Por qué hicimos esto? Dejamos ir a los israelitas, ¡y ahora hemos perdido a nuestros esclavos!».

fr.L: Et on rapporta au roi d’Égypte que le peuple avait fui, et le cœur de Pharaon et de ses serviteurs se tourna contre le peuple, et ils dirent : « Qu’[est-ce] que nous avons fait là, d’avoir laissé Israël partir de notre service ? »
fr.B: La nouvelle parvint au roi d’Égypte que le peuple s’était enfui, et Pharaon et ses ministres se retournèrent contre lui. « Pourquoi avons-nous fait cela ? dirent-ils. Nous avons laissé partir Israël, et il ne nous servira plus ! »
fr.R: Quelqu’un a dit au roi d’Égypte que les Israélites s’étaient enfuis. Alors Pharaon et ses ministres se sont retournés contre eux. Ils ont dit : « Pourquoi avons-nous fait cela ? Nous avons laissé partir les Israélites, et maintenant nous avons perdu nos esclaves ! »

sw.L: Naye mfalme wa Misri akaambiwa kwamba watu wamekimbia, na moyo wa Farao na wa watumishi wake ukageuka juu ya watu, wakasema, "Ni nini hiki tulichofanya, kwamba tumemwacha Israeli aende asitutumikie?"
sw.B: Habari zilimfikia mfalme wa Misri kwamba watu walikuwa wamekimbia, naye Farao pamoja na maafisa wake wakawageuka. Wakasema, "Kwa nini tumefanya hivi? Tumewaacha Israeli waende, nao hawatatutumikia tena!"
sw.R: Mtu mmoja alimwambia mfalme wa Misri kwamba Waisraeli walikuwa wamekimbia. Ndipo Farao na maafisa wake wakawageuka. Wakasema, "Kwa nini tumefanya hivi? Tumewaacha Waisraeli waende, na sasa tumewapoteza watumwa wetu!"

decisions.choice: fled: gone for good
decisions.reason: Pharaoh had sent Israel out (12:31-32), and earlier the request had been for a journey of three days to worship (5:3). The report that the people have "fled" means that they are not coming back.

decisions.choice: the heart was turned: they changed their minds
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will. Their heart toward the people "turned": they regretted letting Israel go and turned against them.

decisions.choice: let Israel go from serving us: released them, so they no longer serve us
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's loss is a loss of labor. The word "serve" is the one God used: Israel was to go "that they may serve me" (9:1).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" are his court and officials (5:21; 11:3). Balanced and Readable say "officials"; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: our slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" in Readable, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt: Egypt has lost the people it held in bondage.

source.text: וַיֶּאְסֹ֖ר אֶת־רִכְבּ֑וֹ וְאֶת־עַמּ֖וֹ לָקַ֥ח עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he harnessed his chariot, and his people he took with him.

en.L: And he harnessed his chariot and took his people with him.
en.B: Then Pharaoh had his chariot harnessed and took his troops along.
en.R: So Pharaoh had his war chariot hitched up, and he gathered his army to go with him.

es.L: Y unció su carro y tomó consigo a su pueblo.
es.B: Entonces el faraón hizo enganchar su carro y llevó consigo a sus tropas.
es.R: Así que el faraón mandó preparar su carro de guerra y reunió a su ejército para que fuera con él.

fr.L: Et il attela son char et prit son peuple avec lui.
fr.B: Alors Pharaon fit atteler son char et emmena ses troupes.
fr.R: Pharaon a donc fait préparer son char de guerre, et il a rassemblé son armée pour partir avec lui.

sw.L: Naye akalifunga gari lake la vita, akawachukua watu wake pamoja naye.
sw.B: Kisha Farao aliamuru gari lake la vita liandaliwe, akaenda pamoja na majeshi yake.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Farao aliagiza gari lake la vita liandaliwe, akakusanya jeshi lake liende pamoja naye.

decisions.choice: his people: his fighting men, his army
decisions.reason: "People" here means the men under arms, as in Numbers 20:20, where Edom comes out with "many people".

decisions.choice: he harnessed: he had it harnessed
decisions.reason: A king gives the order; the verb says what was done at his command.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he"; Balanced and Readable name Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: "gari la vita" (war chariot), "magari ya vita", here and through the chapter
decisions.reason: "Gari" alone today means a car or any vehicle, so the first mention says "gari la vita", a horse-drawn chariot for war (see the note at verse 7); later mentions say "magari" where the context is clear.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֗ח שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת רֶ֨כֶב֙ בָּח֔וּר וְכֹ֖ל רֶ֣כֶב מִצְרָ֑יִם וְשָׁלִשִׁ֖ם עַל־כֻּלּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took six hundred chariots chosen, and all [the] chariotry of Egypt, and officers over all of it.

en.L: And he took 600 chosen chariots, and all the chariotry of Egypt, and officers over all of it.
en.B: He took 600 picked chariots and the rest of Egypt's chariot force too, with officers over the whole of it.
en.R: He took his 600 best chariots. He also took every other chariot in Egypt. Officers were in charge of all of them.

es.L: Y tomó 600 carros escogidos, y todos los carros de Egipto, y oficiales sobre todos ellos.
es.B: Tomó 600 carros selectos y el resto de los carros de guerra de Egipto, con oficiales al mando de todos ellos.
es.R: Tomó sus 600 mejores carros. También tomó todos los demás carros de Egipto. Había oficiales al mando de todos ellos.

fr.L: Et il prit 600 chars d’élite, et tous les chars de l’Égypte, et des officiers sur l’ensemble.
fr.B: Il prit 600 chars d’élite et le reste des chars d’Égypte, avec des officiers à la tête de tous.
fr.R: Il a pris ses 600 meilleurs chars. Il a aussi pris tous les autres chars d’Égypte. Des officiers commandaient l’ensemble.

sw.L: Akachukua magari 600 yaliyochaguliwa, na magari yote ya vita ya Misri, na maafisa juu ya yote.
sw.B: Alichukua magari 600 ya vita yaliyochaguliwa, pamoja na magari mengine yote ya Misri, na maafisa wakiyasimamia yote.
sw.R: Alichukua magari yake 600 ya vita yaliyo bora kuliko yote. Pia alichukua magari mengine yote ya vita ya Misri. Maafisa waliyaongoza yote.

decisions.choice: officers: high-ranking soldiers in the chariot force
alternatives: third men (a third man in each chariot)
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for "three". It may name the third man in a chariot, beside the driver and the fighter, or an officer of high rank (2 Kings 9:25; 10:25). Either way, the chariots went out with their commanders.

decisions.choice: all the chariotry of Egypt: the rest of the chariots, besides the 600 chosen ones
decisions.reason: The 600 picked chariots led the way, and the rest of Egypt's chariots went with them. Chariots were light, horse-drawn vehicles for war, the fastest and strongest part of Egypt's army.

source.text: וַיְחַזֵּ֣ק יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶת־לֵ֤ב פַּרְעֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יֹצְאִ֖ים בְּיָ֥ד רָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And made strong Yahweh [the] heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after [the] sons of Israel, and [the] sons of Israel [were] going out with a hand high.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt strong, and he pursued after the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel were going out with a high hand.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the heart of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, stubborn, and he went after the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, who were leaving with heads held high.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, stubborn. So Pharaoh chased the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, who were leaving boldly.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} fortaleció el corazón del faraón, rey de Egipto, y él persiguió a los hijos de Israel; y los hijos de Israel salían con mano alzada.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} endureció el corazón del faraón, rey de Egipto, y este salió tras los israelitas, que se marchaban con la frente en alto.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo que el faraón, rey de Egipto, se pusiera terco. Así que el faraón persiguió a los israelitas, que se iban con valentía.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} rendit fort le cœur de Pharaon, roi d’Égypte, et il poursuivit les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël ; et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël sortaient la main levée.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} rendit obstiné le cœur de Pharaon, roi d’Égypte, et celui-ci se lança à la poursuite des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, qui partaient la tête haute.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a rendu têtu Pharaon, le roi d’Égypte. Alors Pharaon a poursuivi les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, qui partaient avec assurance.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akautia nguvu moyo wa Farao mfalme wa Misri, naye akawafuatia wana wa Israeli; nao wana wa Israeli walikuwa wakitoka kwa mkono ulioinuliwa.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliufanya moyo wa Farao, mfalme wa Misri, kuwa mgumu, naye akawafuata Waisraeli, waliokuwa wakiondoka vichwa vyao vikiwa juu.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimfanya Farao, mfalme wa Misri, kuwa mkaidi. Kwa hiyo Farao aliwafuatia Waisraeli, waliokuwa wakiondoka kwa ujasiri.

decisions.choice: Yahweh made Pharaoh's heart strong: as God said in verse 4
decisions.reason: See the note at 7:3.

decisions.choice: with a high hand: boldly, openly
alternatives: under the power of God's raised hand
decisions.reason: A raised hand is a sign of strength and confidence. Israel left in the open, without fear (Numbers 33:3 says the same of the night they left, "in the sight of all the Egyptians"). The phrase may also point to God's power: the raised hand would then be the hand of God that brought them out (6:1; 13:9). In Numbers 15:30 the same phrase means "defiantly".

decisions.choice: with heads held high (Balanced); boldly (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an English picture of confidence for the Hebrew one; Readable says what it means. Literal keeps "with a high hand".

source.text: וַיִּרְדְּפ֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם וַיַּשִּׂ֤יגוּ אוֹתָם֙ חֹנִ֣ים עַל־הַיָּ֔ם כָּל־סוּס֙ רֶ֣כֶב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וּפָרָשָׁ֖יו וְחֵיל֑וֹ עַל־פִּי֙ הַֽחִירֹ֔ת לִפְנֵ֖י בַּ֥עַל צְפֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And pursued Egypt after them and overtook them camping by the sea, every horse of [the] chariotry of Pharaoh and his horsemen and his army, beside Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.

en.L: And the Egyptians pursued after them and overtook them camping by the sea, every horse of Pharaoh's chariotry and his horsemen and his army, beside Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.
en.B: The Egyptians, all Pharaoh's chariot horses, his horsemen and his army, went after them and caught up with them where they were camped by the sea, beside Pi-hahiroth, facing Baal-zephon.
en.R: The Egyptians chased after the Israelites with all of Pharaoh's chariot horses, his horsemen, and his army. They caught up with the Israelites while they were camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth, across from Baal-zephon.

es.L: Y los egipcios los persiguieron, y los alcanzaron acampados junto al mar, todos los caballos de los carros del faraón y sus jinetes y su ejército, junto a Pi-hahirot, delante de Baal-zefón.
es.B: Los egipcios, con todos los caballos de los carros del faraón, sus jinetes y su ejército, salieron tras ellos y los alcanzaron donde estaban acampados junto al mar, al lado de Pi-hahirot, frente a Baal-zefón.
es.R: Los egipcios persiguieron a los israelitas con todos los caballos de los carros del faraón, sus jinetes y su ejército. Los alcanzaron mientras estaban acampados junto al mar, cerca de Pi-hahirot, frente a Baal-zefón.

fr.L: Et les Égyptiens les poursuivirent et les rattrapèrent campés près de la mer, tous les chevaux des chars de Pharaon, et ses cavaliers et son armée, près de Pi-Hahiroth, devant Baal-Tsephôn.
fr.B: Les Égyptiens, tous les chevaux des chars de Pharaon, ses cavaliers et son armée, se lancèrent à leur poursuite et les rejoignirent là où ils campaient au bord de la mer, près de Pi-Hahiroth, face à Baal-Tsephôn.
fr.R: Les Égyptiens ont poursuivi les Israélites avec tous les chevaux des chars de Pharaon, ses cavaliers et son armée. Ils les ont rattrapés pendant qu’ils campaient au bord de la mer, près de Pi-Hahiroth, en face de Baal-Tsephôn.

sw.L: Nao Wamisri wakawafuatia, wakawapata wamepiga kambi kando ya bahari, farasi wote wa magari ya Farao, na wapanda farasi wake, na jeshi lake, karibu na Pi-hahirothi, mbele ya Baal-sefoni.
sw.B: Wamisri, yaani farasi wote wa magari ya Farao, wapanda farasi wake na jeshi lake, waliwafuatia, wakawakuta mahali walipopiga kambi kando ya bahari, karibu na Pi-hahirothi, mkabala na Baal-sefoni.
sw.R: Wamisri waliwafuatia Waisraeli wakiwa na farasi wote wa magari ya Farao, wapanda farasi wake na jeshi lake. Waliwafikia Waisraeli walipokuwa wamepiga kambi kando ya bahari, karibu na Pi-hahirothi, mkabala na Baal-sefoni.

decisions.choice: horsemen: the men who drove and fought from the chariots, or riders on horseback
decisions.reason: The word can mean riders, or the horses themselves, or the crews of chariots. Egypt's army at this time fought mainly from chariots, so the "horsemen" may be the chariot crews.

decisions.choice: every horse of Pharaoh's chariotry ...: the list says who "Egypt" was
decisions.reason: The list of horses, horsemen and army stands after the verbs and spells out the force that pursued Israel.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: "Egypt" here is the Egyptian army, as often in this chapter, so every level says "the Egyptians".

source.text: וּפַרְעֹ֖ה הִקְרִ֑יב וַיִּשְׂאוּ֩ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶ֜ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה מִצְרַ֣יִם׀נֹסֵ֣עַ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם וַיִּֽירְאוּ֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַיִּצְעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Pharaoh drew near, and lifted up [the] sons of Israel their eyes, and look, Egypt [was] marching after them, and they feared greatly, and cried out [the] sons of Israel to Yahweh.

en.L: And Pharaoh drew near, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel lifted up their eyes, and look, the Egyptians [were] marching after them, and they feared greatly, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Pharaoh was drawing closer. When the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} looked up, they saw the Egyptians advancing behind them, and they were filled with fear. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Pharaoh and his army came closer. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} looked up and saw the Egyptians coming after them. They were very afraid, and they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help.

es.L: Y el faraón se acercó, y los hijos de Israel alzaron sus ojos, y he aquí que los egipcios marchaban tras ellos; y tuvieron mucho miedo, y los hijos de Israel clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: El faraón se iba acercando. Cuando los israelitas alzaron la vista, vieron a los egipcios que avanzaban detrás de ellos, y se llenaron de temor. Los israelitas clamaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: El faraón y su ejército se acercaron. Los israelitas miraron y vieron que los egipcios venían tras ellos. Tuvieron mucho miedo y le pidieron ayuda a gritos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et Pharaon s’approcha, et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël levèrent les yeux, et voici que les Égyptiens marchaient derrière eux ; et ils eurent très peur, et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël crièrent vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Pharaon approchait. Quand les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} levèrent les yeux, ils virent les Égyptiens qui avançaient derrière eux, et ils furent saisis de crainte. Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} crièrent vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Pharaon et son armée se sont approchés. Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont levé les yeux et ont vu les Égyptiens qui venaient derrière eux. Ils ont eu très peur, et ils ont crié vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les aide.

sw.L: Naye Farao alipokaribia, wana wa Israeli wakainua macho yao, na tazama, Wamisri walikuwa wakiwafuata nyuma yao; wakaogopa sana, nao wana wa Israeli wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Farao alikuwa akikaribia. Waisraeli walipoinua macho, waliwaona Wamisri wakija nyuma yao, wakajaa hofu. Waisraeli wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Farao na jeshi lake walikaribia. Waisraeli walitazama, wakawaona Wamisri wakiwafuata. Waliogopa sana, wakamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awasaidie.

decisions.choice: cried out: the cry of people in distress
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the Israelites crying out under their slave drivers (5:8, 15), and its noun is the "cry" God heard in 3:7, 9. It is a call for help.

decisions.choice: lifted up their eyes: looked up and saw
decisions.reason: The phrase introduces what someone sees (Genesis 22:4, 13).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh and his army ... for help
decisions.reason: Readable says that Pharaoh came with his army (verse 9) and that the cry was a call for help.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֒ הַֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין־קְבָרִים֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם לְקַחְתָּ֖נוּ לָמ֣וּת בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר מַה־זֹּאת֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֔נוּ לְהוֹצִיאָ֖נוּ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to Moses, [is it] from there being no graves in Egypt [that] you have taken us to die in the wilderness? What [is] this you have done to us, to bring us out from Egypt?

en.L: And they said to Moses, "Is it because there are no graves in Egypt [that] you have taken us to die in the wilderness? What [is] this you have done to us, to bring us out of Egypt?
en.B: They said to Moses, "Did Egypt have no graves, that you had to bring us out here to die in the wilderness? What a thing to do to us, leading us out of Egypt!
en.R: They said to Moses, "Why did you bring us out here to die in the desert? Were there not enough graves for us in Egypt? Look at what you have done to us by taking us out of Egypt!

es.L: Y dijeron a Moisés: «¿Es porque no hay sepulcros en Egipto [que] nos has traído para morir en el desierto? ¿Qué [es] esto que nos has hecho, sacándonos de Egipto?
es.B: Le dijeron a Moisés: «¿Acaso no había tumbas en Egipto, que tuviste que traernos aquí a morir en el desierto? ¡Qué cosa nos has hecho, sacándonos de Egipto!
es.R: Le dijeron a Moisés: «¿Por qué nos trajiste aquí a morir en el desierto? ¿No había suficientes tumbas para nosotros en Egipto? ¡Mira lo que nos has hecho al sacarnos de Egipto!

fr.L: Et ils dirent à Moïse : « Est-ce parce qu’il n’y a pas de tombeaux en Égypte [que] tu nous as emmenés mourir dans le désert ? Qu’[est-ce] que tu nous as fait là, en nous faisant sortir d’Égypte ?
fr.B: Ils dirent à Moïse : « N’y avait-il donc pas de tombeaux en Égypte, pour que tu nous amènes mourir ici, dans le désert ? Voilà ce que tu nous as fait en nous emmenant hors d’Égypte !
fr.R: Ils ont dit à Moïse : « Pourquoi nous as-tu amenés mourir ici, dans le désert ? Il n’y avait pas assez de tombes pour nous en Égypte ? Regarde ce que tu nous as fait en nous faisant sortir d’Égypte !

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia Musa, "Je, ni kwa sababu hapakuwa na makaburi Misri [ndipo] umetuleta tufe nyikani? Ni nini hiki ulichotutendea, kwa kututoa Misri?
sw.B: Wakamwambia Musa, "Je, Misri hapakuwa na makaburi, hata ukatuleta huku tufe nyikani? Ni jambo gani hili ulilotutendea, kututoa Misri!
sw.R: Walimwambia Musa, "Kwa nini umetuleta huku tufe jangwani? Je, hapakuwa na makaburi ya kutosha kwa ajili yetu huko Misri? Tazama ulichotufanyia kwa kututoa Misri!

decisions.choice: are there no graves in Egypt?: a bitter, mocking question
decisions.reason: The question is ironic. Egypt was famous for its tombs, and the people say they might as well have died and been buried there as die unburied in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: what is this you have done to us?: a reproach
decisions.reason: The question blames Moses. It echoes Pharaoh's own question in verse 5: both sides now regret the exodus.

decisions.choice: two questions in reverse order
decisions.reason: Readable puts the plain complaint first and the ironic question second, so the irony is easier to follow.

source.text: הֲלֹא־זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבַּ֨רְנוּ אֵלֶ֤יךָ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר חֲדַ֥ל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ וְנַֽעַבְדָ֣ה אֶת־מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּ֣י ט֥וֹב לָ֨נוּ֙ עֲבֹ֣ד אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם מִמֻּתֵ֖נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] not this the word which we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, cease from us, that we may serve Egypt? For [it is] good for us to serve Egypt more than our dying in the wilderness.

en.L: [Is] not this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, 'Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians'? For better for us [is] serving the Egyptians than our dying in the wilderness."
en.B: Did we not tell you this very thing back in Egypt? We said, 'Let us be, and we will serve the Egyptians.' Serving the Egyptians was better for us than dying here in the wilderness!"
en.R: Back in Egypt we told you, 'Leave us alone! Let us go on working for the Egyptians.' Working as slaves for the Egyptians would be better than dying out here in the desert!"

es.L: ¿No [es] esta la palabra que te dijimos en Egipto, diciendo: “Déjanos en paz, que sirvamos a los egipcios”? Porque mejor nos [es] servir a los egipcios que morir nosotros en el desierto».
es.B: ¿No te dijimos esto mismo allá en Egipto? Te dijimos: “Déjanos tranquilos, y serviremos a los egipcios”. ¡Era mejor para nosotros servir a los egipcios que morir aquí en el desierto!».
es.R: Allá en Egipto te dijimos: “¡Déjanos en paz! Déjanos seguir trabajando para los egipcios”. ¡Sería mejor trabajar como esclavos para los egipcios que morir aquí en el desierto!».

fr.L: N’[est-ce] pas là la parole que nous t’avons dite en Égypte, en disant : “Laisse-nous, que nous servions les Égyptiens” ? Car mieux vaut pour nous servir les Égyptiens que mourir dans le désert. »
fr.B: Ne te l’avions-nous pas dit en Égypte ? Nous disions : “Laisse-nous tranquilles, nous servirons les Égyptiens.” Il valait mieux pour nous servir les Égyptiens que mourir ici, dans le désert ! »
fr.R: En Égypte, nous t’avions dit : “Laisse-nous tranquilles ! Laisse-nous continuer à travailler pour les Égyptiens.” Ce serait mieux de travailler comme esclaves pour les Égyptiens que de mourir ici, dans le désert ! »

sw.L: Je, hili [si] neno lile tulilokuambia huko Misri, tukisema, 'Tuache, tuwatumikie Wamisri'? Kwa maana ni afadhali kwetu kuwatumikia Wamisri kuliko kufa kwetu nyikani."
sw.B: Je, hatukukuambia jambo hili hasa tulipokuwa Misri? Tulisema, 'Tuache, nasi tutawatumikia Wamisri.' Ingekuwa afadhali kwetu kuwatumikia Wamisri kuliko kufa huku nyikani!"
sw.R: Tulipokuwa Misri tulikuambia, 'Tuache! Tuendelee kuwafanyia Wamisri kazi.' Ingekuwa afadhali kuwa watumwa wa Wamisri kuliko kufa huku jangwani!"

decisions.choice: the word we spoke to you in Egypt: their earlier complaints
decisions.reason: These words are not recorded earlier, but the people's earlier response is: the foremen blamed Moses and Aaron (5:21), and the people would not listen to Moses because of their hard labor (6:9).

decisions.choice: serve the Egyptians: work as their slaves
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used throughout Exodus for serving God (9:1). Under threat, the people would rather serve Egypt than go free to serve God.

decisions.choice: working for / working as slaves for
decisions.reason: Readable says what serving Egypt meant; Literal and Balanced keep "serve", the word used for serving God. "Slaves" stays, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל־הָעָם֮ אַל־תִּירָאוּ֒ הִֽתְיַצְב֗וּ וּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־יְשׁוּעַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם כִּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר רְאִיתֶ֤ם אֶת־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ הַיּ֔וֹם לֹ֥א תֹסִ֛יפוּ לִרְאֹתָ֥ם ע֖וֹד עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to the people, do not fear. Station yourselves and see [the] salvation of Yahweh, which he will do for you today; for [the] Egypt which you have seen today, not you will again see them any more until forever.

en.L: And Moses said to the people, "Do not fear. Station yourselves and see the salvation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do for you today; for the Egyptians whom you have seen today, you will not see them again any more, forever.
en.B: But Moses told the people, "Have no fear! Hold your ground and watch how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will save you today. You see the Egyptians today, but you will never see them again.
en.R: Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid. Stay where you are, and you will see {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rescue you today. You will never see these Egyptians again.

es.L: Y Moisés dijo al pueblo: «No {{plural_you:teman|temáis}}. {{plural_you:Manténganse|Manteneos}} firmes y {{plural_you:vean|ved}} la salvación {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hará hoy por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; porque a los egipcios que hoy {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}}, no los {{plural_you:volverán|volveréis}} a ver nunca más.
es.B: Pero Moisés le dijo al pueblo: «¡No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo! {{plural_you:Manténganse|Manteneos}} firmes y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} cómo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:los|os}} va a salvar hoy. Hoy {{plural_you:ven|veis}} a los egipcios, pero nunca más {{plural_you:volverán|volveréis}} a verlos.
es.R: Moisés le dijo al pueblo: «No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. {{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} donde {{plural_you:están|estáis}}, y {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} cómo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:los|os}} rescata hoy. Nunca más {{plural_you:volverán|volveréis}} a ver a estos egipcios.

fr.L: Et Moïse dit au peuple : « N’ayez pas peur. Tenez-vous là et voyez le salut {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} accomplira pour vous aujourd’hui ; car les Égyptiens que vous avez vus aujourd’hui, vous ne les reverrez plus jamais.
fr.B: Mais Moïse dit au peuple : « N’ayez aucune crainte ! Tenez bon, et regardez comment {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va vous sauver aujourd’hui. Vous voyez les Égyptiens aujourd’hui, mais vous ne les reverrez jamais plus.
fr.R: Moïse a dit au peuple : « N’ayez pas peur. Restez où vous êtes, et vous verrez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous délivrer aujourd’hui. Vous ne reverrez plus jamais ces Égyptiens.

sw.L: Naye Musa akawaambia watu, "Msiogope. Simameni imara mkauone wokovu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, atakaowatendea leo; kwa maana Wamisri hao mliowaona leo hamtawaona tena kamwe, hata milele.
sw.B: Lakini Musa akawaambia watu, "Msiwe na hofu! Simameni imara, mtazame jinsi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakavyowaokoa leo. Mnawaona Wamisri leo, lakini hamtawaona tena kamwe.
sw.R: Musa aliwaambia watu, "Msiogope. Kaeni hapo hapo, nanyi mtamwona {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akiwaokoa leo. Hamtawaona tena Wamisri hawa.

decisions.choice: the salvation of Yahweh: Yahweh's rescue from danger
decisions.reason: The noun means rescue or deliverance, help that saves people from a threat they cannot escape. It comes from the verb "save" in verse 30, where the rescue is done. Israel will sing, "He has become my salvation" (15:2).

decisions.choice: station yourselves: stand firm, hold your position
decisions.reason: The verb means to take one's stand and stay there. The people are not to run or fight but to stand and watch what God does.

decisions.choice: you will not see them again: never again as a threat
decisions.reason: The emphatic "not ... again ... forever" promises an end to the danger. Israel does see the Egyptians once more, dead on the shore (verse 30).

decisions.choice: watch how the LORD will save you (Balanced); see the LORD rescue you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a verb, with God as its subject. Balanced keeps the word family of "salvation" ("save"); Readable says "rescue", the plain sense. Literal keeps "the salvation of the LORD".

source.text: יְהוָ֖ה יִלָּחֵ֣ם לָכֶ֑ם וְאַתֶּ֖ם תַּחֲרִישֽׁוּן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh will fight for you, and you, you will keep silent.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will fight for you, and you, you will keep silent."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will fight on your behalf, and you can stay quiet."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will fight for you. All you have to do is stay calm."

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} peleará por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:guardarán|guardaréis}} silencio».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} peleará en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} favor, y {{plural_you:ustedes pueden quedarse|vosotros podéis quedaros}} tranquilos».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} peleará por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Lo único que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que hacer es mantener la calma».

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} combattra pour vous, et vous, vous garderez le silence. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} combattra à votre place, et vous pourrez rester tranquilles. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va combattre pour vous. Vous, restez simplement calmes. »

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atawapigania, nanyi mtanyamaza kimya."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atapigana kwa ajili yenu, nanyi mnaweza kukaa kimya."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atawapigania. Ninyi kaeni tu kwa utulivu."

decisions.choice: Yahweh will fight for you: God as the warrior who defends his people
decisions.reason: Israel will not fight; Yahweh will. In verse 25 the Egyptians themselves say it, and Israel sings, "Yahweh is a man of war" (15:3).

decisions.choice: keep silent: be still, do nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to be quiet. Set against "Yahweh will fight", it means to stop crying out and complaining and to leave the battle to God.

decisions.choice: stay calm
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of keeping silent here: not panicking, waiting for God to act.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה מַה־תִּצְעַ֖ק אֵלָ֑י דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל־בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְיִסָּֽעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, why do you cry out to me? Speak to [the] sons of Israel, that they set out.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Why do you cry out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, that they set out.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Why are you crying out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to break camp and go forward.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Why are you calling to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for help? Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to start moving.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «¿Por qué clamas a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}? Di a los hijos de Israel que se pongan en marcha.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} estás clamando? Diles a los israelitas que levanten el campamento y sigan adelante.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pides ayuda a gritos? Diles a los israelitas que se pongan en camino.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Pourquoi cries-tu vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ? Parle aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, qu’ils partent.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Pourquoi cries-tu vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ? Dis aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} de lever le camp et d’aller de l’avant.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appelles-tu à l’aide ? Dis aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} de se mettre en route.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Mbona unalia {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}? Sema na wana wa Israeli, waondoke.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Kwa nini unanililia? Waambie Waisraeli wavunje kambi, waendelee mbele.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Kwa nini unaniita ili nikusaidie? Waambie Waisraeli waanze kuondoka.

decisions.choice: why do you cry out to me?: the time for prayer has given way to action
alternatives: Moses had cried out on the people's behalf
decisions.reason: Moses' own cry is not recorded. He may have cried out with the people (verse 10), or he may be addressed as their leader, speaking for them. God's question is not a rebuke of prayer but a call to move.

decisions.choice: set out: break camp and move on
decisions.reason: The verb means to pull up the tent pegs and travel on, as at each stage of the journey (12:37; 13:20).

decisions.choice: break camp and go forward
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out the two parts of the verb: leaving the camp and moving on toward the sea.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֞ה הָרֵ֣ם אֶֽת־מַטְּךָ֗ וּנְטֵ֧ה אֶת־יָדְךָ֛ עַל־הַיָּ֖ם וּבְקָעֵ֑הוּ וְיָבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּ֖ם בַּיַּבָּשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and split it, that may go [the] sons of Israel in [the] midst of the sea on dry ground.

en.L: And you, raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and split it, that the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel may go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.
en.B: As for you, lift up your staff, reach out your hand over the sea, and split it open, so that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} can walk through the middle of the sea on dry ground.
en.R: Hold up your staff and reach your hand out over the sea. Split the sea in two, and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will walk across the middle of it on dry ground.

es.L: Y tú, alza tu vara y extiende tu mano sobre el mar y divídelo, para que los hijos de Israel entren por en medio del mar sobre tierra seca.
es.B: Tú, levanta tu vara, extiende tu mano sobre el mar y ábrelo en dos, para que los israelitas puedan pasar por en medio del mar sobre tierra seca.
es.R: Levanta tu vara y extiende tu mano sobre el mar. Divide el mar en dos, y los israelitas cruzarán por el medio sobre tierra seca.

fr.L: Et toi, lève ton bâton et étends ta main sur la mer et fends-la, afin que les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël entrent au milieu de la mer sur la terre sèche.
fr.B: Quant à toi, lève ton bâton, étends ta main sur la mer et ouvre-la en deux, afin que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} puissent passer au milieu de la mer à pied sec.
fr.R: Lève ton bâton et tends la main au-dessus de la mer. Fends la mer en deux, et les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} traverseront au milieu, sur un sol sec.

sw.L: Nawe, inua fimbo yako, unyoshe mkono wako juu ya bahari, uipasue, ili wana wa Israeli waingie katikati ya bahari juu ya nchi kavu.
sw.B: Na wewe, inua fimbo yako, unyoshe mkono wako juu ya bahari, uigawanye, ili Waisraeli waweze kupita katikati ya bahari juu ya nchi kavu.
sw.R: Inua fimbo yako, unyoshe mkono wako juu ya bahari. Igawanye bahari sehemu mbili, nao Waisraeli watapita katikati yake juu ya nchi kavu.

decisions.choice: split it: divide the sea in two
decisions.reason: The verb means to split or cleave. It is used again of the waters in verse 21 (Psalm 78:13; Nehemiah 9:11).

decisions.choice: dry ground: the word used for the dry land of creation
decisions.reason: The word is the one used when the dry land first appeared from the waters (Genesis 1:9-10). It is used again in verses 22 and 29.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִ֤י מְחַזֵּק֙ אֶת־לֵ֣ב מִצְרַ֔יִם וְיָבֹ֖אוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל־חֵיל֔וֹ בְּרִכְבּ֖וֹ וּבְפָרָשָֽׁיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, look, I [am] about to make strong [the] heart of Egypt, and they will go after them, and I will get glory by Pharaoh and by all his army, by his chariots and by his horsemen.

en.L: And I, look, I am about to make the heart of the Egyptians strong, and they will go in after them, and I will get glory over Pharaoh and over all his army, over his chariots and over his horsemen.
en.B: As for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I am going to make the Egyptians stubborn, so that they follow them in. Then I will win glory at the expense of Pharaoh and his whole army, his chariots and his horsemen.
en.R: I will make the Egyptians stubborn, and they will follow the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} into the sea. Then I will defeat Pharaoh, his whole army, his chariots, and his horsemen, and that will bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glory.

es.L: Y yo, he aquí, yo voy a fortalecer el corazón de los egipcios, y entrarán tras ellos, y obtendré gloria sobre el faraón y sobre todo su ejército, sobre sus carros y sobre sus jinetes.
es.B: En cuanto a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, voy a endurecer el corazón de los egipcios para que entren tras ellos. Entonces obtendré gloria a costa del faraón y de todo su ejército, de sus carros y de sus jinetes.
es.R: Haré que los egipcios se pongan tercos, y seguirán a los israelitas dentro del mar. Entonces derrotaré al faraón, a todo su ejército, a sus carros y a sus jinetes, y eso {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dará gloria.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, voici que je vais rendre fort le cœur des Égyptiens, et ils entreront derrière eux, et je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glorifierai aux dépens de Pharaon et de toute son armée, de ses chars et de ses cavaliers.
fr.B: Quant à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vais rendre les Égyptiens obstinés, pour qu’ils les suivent. Alors je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} couvrirai de gloire aux dépens de Pharaon et de toute son armée, de ses chars et de ses cavaliers.
fr.R: Je rendrai les Égyptiens têtus, et ils suivront les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} dans la mer. Alors je vaincrai Pharaon, toute son armée, ses chars et ses cavaliers, et cela {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} donnera de la gloire.

sw.L: Na {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, tazama, nitaitia nguvu mioyo ya Wamisri, nao wataingia nyuma yao, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitajipatia utukufu juu ya Farao na juu ya jeshi lake lote, juu ya magari yake na juu ya wapanda farasi wake.
sw.B: Kwa upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, nitaifanya mioyo ya Wamisri kuwa migumu, ili wawafuate ndani. Kisha nitajipatia utukufu kupitia Farao na jeshi lake lote, magari yake na wapanda farasi wake.
sw.R: Nitawafanya Wamisri kuwa wakaidi, nao watawafuata Waisraeli baharini. Kisha nitamshinda Farao, jeshi lake lote, magari yake na wapanda farasi wake, na jambo hilo litaniletea utukufu.

decisions.choice: I will make the heart of the Egyptians strong: the whole army is now hardened
decisions.reason: Until now God hardened Pharaoh's heart (verses 4, 8). Now the Egyptians as a whole will be made bold enough to follow Israel into the sea. See the note at 7:3.

decisions.choice: I will get glory: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: The verb from the root "heavy" again: God will be honored through the defeat of Pharaoh and his forces. The "heavy" heart (7:14) meets God's weight.

decisions.choice: into the sea ... I will defeat
decisions.reason: Readable says where the Egyptians will follow Israel and how God will win glory, as in verse 4.

source.text: וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּהִכָּבְדִ֣י בְּפַרְעֹ֔ה בְּרִכְבּ֖וֹ וּבְפָרָשָֽׁיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And will know Egypt that I [am] Yahweh, when I get glory by Pharaoh, by his chariots and by his horsemen.

en.L: And the Egyptians will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I get glory over Pharaoh, over his chariots, and over his horsemen."
en.B: The Egyptians will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when I have won glory at the expense of Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen."
en.R: When I defeat Pharaoh and his chariots and horsemen, it will bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glory. Then the Egyptians will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

es.L: Y sabrán los egipcios que yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, cuando obtenga gloria sobre el faraón, sobre sus carros y sobre sus jinetes».
es.B: Los egipcios sabrán que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} cuando haya obtenido gloria a costa del faraón, de sus carros y de sus jinetes».
es.R: Cuando derrote al faraón y a sus carros y jinetes, eso {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dará gloria. Entonces los egipcios sabrán que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».

fr.L: Et les Égyptiens sauront que je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, quand je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glorifierai aux dépens de Pharaon, de ses chars et de ses cavaliers. »
fr.B: Les Égyptiens sauront que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, quand je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} serai couvert de gloire aux dépens de Pharaon, de ses chars et de ses cavaliers. »
fr.R: Quand je vaincrai Pharaon, ses chars et ses cavaliers, cela {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} donnera de la gloire. Alors les Égyptiens sauront que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: Nao Wamisri watajua ya kuwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakapojipatia utukufu juu ya Farao, juu ya magari yake na juu ya wapanda farasi wake."
sw.B: Wamisri watajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndimi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakapokuwa nimejipatia utukufu kupitia Farao, magari yake na wapanda farasi wake."
sw.R: Nitakapomshinda Farao pamoja na magari yake na wapanda farasi wake, jambo hilo litaniletea utukufu. Ndipo Wamisri watajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

decisions.choice: the Egyptians will know that I am Yahweh: repeated from verse 4
decisions.reason: The repetition marks the purpose of the whole event (7:5).

decisions.choice: the cause first, then the result
decisions.reason: Readable puts God's victory first and what the Egyptians will learn from it second.

source.text: וַיִּסַּ֞ע מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים הַהֹלֵךְ֙ לִפְנֵי֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּסַּ֞ע עַמּ֤וּד הֶֽעָנָן֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּֽעֲמֹ֖ד מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out [the] angel of God, the [one] going before [the] camp of Israel, and he went behind them; and set out [the] pillar of the cloud from before them and stood behind them.

en.L: And the angel of God, who was going before the camp of Israel, set out and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud set out from before them and stood behind them.
en.B: The angel of God, who had been going ahead of Israel's camp, moved and went to the rear, and the pillar of cloud moved from in front of them and took its place behind them.
en.R: The angel of God had been leading the Israelites. Now the angel moved and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from the front and stood behind them.

es.L: Y el ángel de Dios, que iba delante del campamento de Israel, se puso en marcha y fue detrás de ellos; y la columna de nube se movió de delante de ellos y se puso detrás de ellos.
es.B: El ángel de Dios, que había ido delante del campamento de Israel, se movió y pasó a la retaguardia, y la columna de nube se apartó de delante de ellos y se colocó detrás.
es.R: El ángel de Dios había estado guiando a los israelitas. Ahora el ángel se movió y se puso detrás de ellos. La columna de nube también se movió del frente y se colocó detrás de ellos.

fr.L: Et l’ange de Dieu, qui allait devant le camp d’Israël, partit et alla derrière eux ; et la colonne de nuée partit de devant eux et se tint derrière eux.
fr.B: L’ange de Dieu, qui marchait en avant du camp d’Israël, se déplaça et passa à l’arrière ; et la colonne de nuée quitta l’avant et vint se placer derrière eux.
fr.R: L’ange de Dieu guidait les Israélites. Mais à ce moment-là, l’ange s’est déplacé et il est passé derrière eux. La colonne de nuage aussi a quitté l’avant et s’est placée derrière eux.

sw.L: Naye malaika wa Mungu, aliyekuwa akitangulia mbele ya kambi ya Israeli, akaondoka akaenda nyuma yao; nayo nguzo ya wingu ikaondoka mbele yao ikasimama nyuma yao.
sw.B: Malaika wa Mungu, aliyekuwa akitangulia mbele ya kambi ya Israeli, alihama akaenda upande wa nyuma, nayo nguzo ya wingu ikahama kutoka mbele yao ikakaa nyuma yao.
sw.R: Malaika wa Mungu alikuwa akiwaongoza Waisraeli. Sasa malaika huyo alihama, akaenda nyuma yao. Nguzo ya wingu nayo ilihama kutoka mbele, ikasimama nyuma yao.

decisions.choice: the angel of God and the pillar of cloud: God's presence guarding Israel
decisions.reason: In 13:21-22 Yahweh went before Israel in the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire. Here the angel of God and the pillar move together; God himself goes with his people (compare 3:2; 23:20). Now he places himself between them and the enemy.

decisions.choice: the camp of Israel: the whole people on the move
decisions.reason: "Camp" is the people of Israel as a company traveling and camping together. In verse 20 it stands beside "the camp of Egypt", the Egyptian army.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א בֵּ֣ין׀מַחֲנֵ֣ה מִצְרַ֗יִם וּבֵין֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְהִ֤י הֶֽעָנָן֙ וְהַחֹ֔שֶׁךְ וַיָּ֖אֶר אֶת־הַלָּ֑יְלָה וְלֹא־קָרַ֥ב זֶ֛ה אֶל־זֶ֖ה כָּל־הַלָּֽיְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it came between [the] camp of Egypt and between [the] camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night, and not came near this to this all the night.

en.L: And it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night, and the one did not come near the other all the night.
en.B: It came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. The cloud was there, and the darkness, and it lit up the night; and all night long neither camp approached the other.
en.R: It came between the Egyptian camp and the Israelite camp. The cloud brought darkness, and it also gave light in the night. So all night long the two camps did not come near each other.

es.L: Y vino entre el campamento de Egipto y el campamento de Israel; y estaban la nube y la oscuridad, y alumbró la noche, y no se acercó el uno al otro en toda la noche.
es.B: Se interpuso entre el campamento de Egipto y el campamento de Israel. Allí estaban la nube y la oscuridad, y alumbraba la noche; y en toda la noche ninguno de los dos campamentos se acercó al otro.
es.R: Se puso entre el campamento egipcio y el campamento israelita. La nube trajo oscuridad, y también dio luz en la noche. Así que en toda la noche los dos campamentos no se acercaron el uno al otro.

fr.L: Et elle vint entre le camp de l’Égypte et le camp d’Israël ; et il y eut la nuée et les ténèbres, et elle illumina la nuit, et l’un ne s’approcha pas de l’autre de toute la nuit.
fr.B: Elle vint se placer entre le camp de l’Égypte et le camp d’Israël. La nuée était là, et les ténèbres, et elle éclairait la nuit ; et de toute la nuit, aucun des deux camps ne s’approcha de l’autre.
fr.R: La colonne s’est placée entre le camp des Égyptiens et le camp des Israélites. Le nuage apportait l’obscurité, mais il éclairait aussi la nuit. Ainsi, de toute la nuit, les deux camps ne se sont pas approchés l’un de l’autre.

sw.L: Ikaingia kati ya kambi ya Misri na kambi ya Israeli; kukawa na lile wingu na giza, nalo likaangaza usiku, wala hii haikuikaribia hii usiku wote.
sw.B: Ilikuja kati ya kambi ya Misri na kambi ya Israeli. Wingu lilikuwepo pamoja na giza, nalo likaangaza usiku; na usiku kucha hakuna kambi iliyoikaribia nyingine.
sw.R: Ilikaa kati ya kambi ya Wamisri na kambi ya Waisraeli. Wingu hilo lilileta giza, na pia lilitoa mwanga usiku. Kwa hiyo usiku kucha kambi hizo mbili hazikukaribiana.

decisions.choice: the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night: the cloud was dark and yet gave light
alternatives: the cloud was dark to the Egyptians and gave light to Israel
and there was darkness and gloom, and the night passed (the Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very brief and hard to read. The most likely sense is that the same cloud brought darkness and also lit up the night, dark toward the Egyptians and bright toward Israel, so the two camps were kept apart. It may also mean that the pillar of fire (13:21) gave light to Israel while the cloud stood dark. The Greek translation reads differently: "and there was darkness and gloom, and the night passed". The translation keeps the Hebrew and its ambiguity.

decisions.choice: this did not come near this: neither camp came near the other
decisions.reason: "This" and "this" are the two camps named at the start of the verse.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨ט מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶת־יָדוֹ֮ עַל־הַיָּם֒ וַיּ֣וֹלֶךְ יְהוָ֣ה׀אֶת־הַ֠יָּם בְּר֨וּחַ קָדִ֤ים עַזָּה֙ כָּל־הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־הַיָּ֖ם לֶחָרָבָ֑ה וַיִּבָּקְע֖וּ הַמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And stretched out Moses his hand over the sea, and drove Yahweh the sea by a wind, east, strong, all the night, and made the sea into dry land, and were split the waters.

en.L: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} drove the sea back by a strong east wind all the night, and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were split.
en.B: Moses held his hand out over the sea, and all night long {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pushed the sea back with a powerful east wind. He turned the sea into dry land, and the waters were split apart.
en.R: Moses held his hand out over the sea. All night long {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pushed the water back with a strong wind from the east. He made the bottom of the sea dry, and the water split apart.

es.L: Y extendió Moisés su mano sobre el mar, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo retroceder el mar con un fuerte viento del este toda la noche, y convirtió el mar en terreno seco, y las aguas se dividieron.
es.B: Moisés extendió su mano sobre el mar, y durante toda la noche {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo retroceder el mar con un poderoso viento del este. Convirtió el mar en terreno seco, y las aguas se partieron en dos.
es.R: Moisés extendió su mano sobre el mar. Durante toda la noche {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} empujó el agua hacia atrás con un fuerte viento que venía del este. Dejó seco el fondo del mar, y el agua se dividió.

fr.L: Et Moïse étendit sa main sur la mer, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} refoula la mer par un fort vent d’est toute la nuit, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fit de la mer un sol asséché, et les eaux se fendirent.
fr.B: Moïse tendit la main au-dessus de la mer, et toute la nuit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} repoussa la mer par un puissant vent d’est. Il changea la mer en sol asséché, et les eaux se séparèrent.
fr.R: Moïse a tendu la main au-dessus de la mer. Pendant toute la nuit, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a repoussé l’eau avec un fort vent qui venait de l’est. Il a asséché le fond de la mer, et l’eau s’est séparée en deux.

sw.L: Naye Musa akaunyosha mkono wake juu ya bahari, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akairudisha bahari nyuma kwa upepo mkali wa mashariki usiku kucha, akaifanya bahari kuwa ardhi kavu, nayo maji yakagawanyika.
sw.B: Musa aliunyosha mkono wake juu ya bahari, na usiku kucha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akairudisha bahari nyuma kwa upepo mkali wa mashariki. Aliigeuza bahari kuwa ardhi kavu, nayo maji yakapasuka sehemu mbili.
sw.R: Musa aliunyosha mkono wake juu ya bahari. Usiku kucha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyasukuma maji nyuma kwa upepo mkali uliovuma kutoka mashariki. Akaifanya sehemu ya chini ya bahari kuwa kavu, nayo maji yakagawanyika.

decisions.choice: a strong east wind: the hot wind from the desert
decisions.reason: An east wind blows from the desert and is hot and drying. It brought the locusts in 10:13. Here God uses it to drive back the sea; Israel's song calls it the blast of God's nostrils (15:8).

decisions.choice: drove: made the sea go back
decisions.reason: The verb is the common word "go" in a form meaning "make go". The sea moved back before the wind.

decisions.choice: dry land: ground with the water gone
decisions.reason: This word means land that has been dried out (Genesis 7:22; Joshua 3:17). Verses 16, 22 and 29 use another word, "dry ground". Both describe the seabed laid bare.

decisions.choice: the bottom of the sea
decisions.reason: Readable says which part of the sea became dry.

decisions.choice: "terreno seco" here; "tierra seca" for the other word in verses 16, 22 and 29
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses two words (m3), as the English "dry land" and "dry ground" show; Spanish keeps them apart with two near expressions.

decisions.choice: "un sol asséché" here; "la terre sèche", "à pied sec" for the other word in verses 16, 22 and 29
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses two words (m3): this one is ground that has been dried out, so French says "asséché" (dried up), keeping it apart from the word for dry ground in verses 16, 22 and 29.

decisions.choice: "ardhi kavu" here; "nchi kavu" for the other word in verses 16, 22 and 29
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses two words (m3), as the English "dry land" and "dry ground" show; Swahili keeps them apart. "Nchi kavu" is the dry land of creation (Genesis 1:9-10), the word the Hebrew of verses 16, 22 and 29 echoes.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּ֖ם בַּיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וְהַמַּ֤יִם לָהֶם֙ חֹמָ֔ה מִֽימִינָ֖ם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went [the] sons of Israel in [the] midst of the sea on dry ground, and the waters [were] to them a wall on their right and on their left.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went into the midst of the sea on dry ground, and the waters [were] a wall to them on their right and on their left.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} went into the middle of the sea on dry ground, and the water was a wall for them, to the right and to the left.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground. The water was like a wall on both sides of them, on the right and on the left.

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel entraron por en medio del mar sobre tierra seca, y las aguas [eran] para ellos un muro a su derecha y a su izquierda.
es.B: Los israelitas entraron en medio del mar sobre tierra seca, y el agua formaba para ellos un muro a la derecha y a la izquierda.
es.R: Los israelitas caminaron por en medio del mar sobre tierra seca. El agua era como una pared a cada lado de ellos, a la derecha y a la izquierda.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël entrèrent au milieu de la mer sur la terre sèche, et les eaux [étaient] pour eux une muraille à leur droite et à leur gauche.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} s’avancèrent au milieu de la mer à pied sec, et l’eau formait pour eux une muraille, à droite et à gauche.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont marché au milieu de la mer sur un sol sec. L’eau était comme un mur des deux côtés, à leur droite et à leur gauche.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakaingia katikati ya bahari juu ya nchi kavu, nayo maji [yalikuwa] ukuta kwao upande wao wa kulia na upande wao wa kushoto.
sw.B: Waisraeli waliingia katikati ya bahari juu ya nchi kavu, nayo maji yakawa ukuta kwao, kulia na kushoto.
sw.R: Waisraeli walitembea katikati ya bahari juu ya nchi kavu. Maji yalikuwa kama ukuta pande zote mbili, kulia na kushoto.

decisions.choice: a wall: a barrier that stood and protected
decisions.reason: A wall is a defense (1 Samuel 25:16, "they were a wall to us"). The waters stood on both sides and kept Israel safe as they crossed. Israel's song says the waters "stood up like a heap" (15:8).

decisions.choice: like a wall
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison so that a young reader takes it as a picture of standing water.

source.text: וַיִּרְדְּפ֤וּ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֚ל ס֣וּס פַּרְעֹ֔ה רִכְבּ֖וֹ וּפָרָשָׁ֑יו אֶל־תּ֖וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And pursued Egypt and went after them, every horse of Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen, into [the] midst of the sea.

en.L: And the Egyptians pursued and went in after them, every horse of Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen, into the midst of the sea.
en.B: The Egyptians gave chase and followed them into the middle of the sea, all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots and his horsemen.
en.R: The Egyptians went after them, right into the middle of the sea. Every one of Pharaoh's horses went in, with his chariots and his horsemen.

es.L: Y los egipcios los persiguieron y entraron tras ellos, todos los caballos del faraón, sus carros y sus jinetes, hasta en medio del mar.
es.B: Los egipcios salieron en su persecución y los siguieron hasta el medio del mar, con todos los caballos del faraón, sus carros y sus jinetes.
es.R: Los egipcios fueron tras ellos, hasta el mismo medio del mar. Entraron todos los caballos del faraón, con sus carros y sus jinetes.

fr.L: Et les Égyptiens les poursuivirent et entrèrent derrière eux, tous les chevaux de Pharaon, ses chars et ses cavaliers, au milieu de la mer.
fr.B: Les Égyptiens se lancèrent à leur poursuite et les suivirent jusqu’au milieu de la mer, tous les chevaux de Pharaon, ses chars et ses cavaliers.
fr.R: Les Égyptiens sont partis après eux, jusqu’au milieu de la mer. Tous les chevaux de Pharaon y sont entrés, avec ses chars et ses cavaliers.

sw.L: Nao Wamisri wakawafuatia, wakaingia nyuma yao, farasi wote wa Farao, magari yake na wapanda farasi wake, mpaka katikati ya bahari.
sw.B: Wamisri waliwafuatia, wakawafuata hadi katikati ya bahari, yaani farasi wote wa Farao, magari yake na wapanda farasi wake.
sw.R: Wamisri waliwafuata, wakaingia mpaka katikati ya bahari. Kila farasi wa Farao aliingia, pamoja na magari yake na wapanda farasi wake.

decisions.choice: they went after them into the midst of the sea: what God said in verse 17
decisions.reason: God said the Egyptians would go in after Israel (verse 17), and they do. The list of horses, chariots and horsemen again shows the whole force.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בְּאַשְׁמֹ֣רֶת הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיַּשְׁקֵ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מַחֲנֵ֣ה מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּעַמּ֥וּד אֵ֖שׁ וְעָנָ֑ן וַיָּ֕הָם אֵ֖ת מַחֲנֵ֥ה מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] watch of the morning, and looked down Yahweh on [the] camp of Egypt in a pillar of fire and cloud, and he threw into panic [the] camp of Egypt.

en.L: And it was in the morning watch, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked down on the camp of Egypt in the pillar of fire and cloud, and threw the camp of Egypt into panic.
en.B: In the last hours of the night, before morning, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked down on the Egyptian camp from the pillar of fire and cloud and threw the camp into panic.
en.R: Just before dawn, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked down at the Egyptian army from the pillar of fire and cloud. He made the Egyptians panic and fall into confusion.

es.L: Y sucedió en la vigilia de la mañana que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} miró desde lo alto hacia el campamento de Egipto, en la columna de fuego y de nube, y sembró el pánico en el campamento de Egipto.
es.B: En las últimas horas de la noche, antes del amanecer, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} miró desde la columna de fuego y de nube hacia el campamento egipcio y llenó de pánico el campamento.
es.R: Poco antes del amanecer, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} miró al ejército egipcio desde la columna de fuego y de nube. Hizo que los egipcios se llenaran de pánico y de confusión.

fr.L: Et il arriva, à la veille du matin, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} regarda d’en haut vers le camp de l’Égypte, dans la colonne de feu et de nuée, et jeta la panique dans le camp de l’Égypte.
fr.B: Dans les dernières heures de la nuit, avant le matin, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} abaissa {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} regard sur le camp égyptien depuis la colonne de feu et de nuée, et y jeta la panique.
fr.R: Juste avant l’aube, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a regardé l’armée égyptienne depuis la colonne de feu et de nuage. Il a fait paniquer les Égyptiens, et ils ont été pris de confusion.

sw.L: Ikawa katika zamu ya alfajiri, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaichungulia kambi ya Misri akiwa katika nguzo ya moto na ya wingu, akaitia hofu kuu kambi ya Misri.
sw.B: Katika saa za mwisho za usiku, kabla ya asubuhi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliitazama kambi ya Wamisri kutoka juu katika nguzo ya moto na wingu, akaitia kambi hiyo hofu kuu.
sw.R: Kabla tu ya mapambazuko, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliliangalia jeshi la Wamisri kutoka katika nguzo ya moto na wingu. Aliwafanya Wamisri washikwe na hofu na kuchanganyikiwa.

decisions.choice: the morning watch: the last part of the night, before dawn
decisions.reason: The night was divided into watches, periods when guards kept watch (Judges 7:19; Lamentations 2:19). The morning watch was the last, ending at daybreak. Israel had crossed during the night (verse 21).

decisions.choice: threw into panic: confused and routed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God throwing an enemy army into confusion and flight (Joshua 10:10; Judges 4:15; 1 Samuel 7:10).

decisions.choice: looked down: looked down from above
decisions.reason: The verb is used of looking down from a height, as God looks down from heaven (Psalm 14:2). From the pillar of fire and cloud, God looked on the Egyptians and acted.

decisions.choice: in the last hours of the night, before morning (Balanced); just before dawn (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the morning watch" was; Literal keeps the term.

source.text: וַיָּ֗סַר אֵ֚ת אֹפַ֣ן מַרְכְּבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיְנַהֲגֵ֖הוּ בִּכְבֵדֻ֑ת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִצְרַ֗יִם אָנ֨וּסָה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה נִלְחָ֥ם לָהֶ֖ם בְּמִצְרָֽיִם

records.literal_gloss: And he removed [the] wheels of his chariots, and he made it drive with heaviness. And said Egypt, let me flee from before Israel, for Yahweh [is] fighting for them against Egypt.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} removed the wheels of their chariots and made them drive with heaviness. And the Egyptians said, "Let us flee from before Israel, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is fighting for them against Egypt."
en.B: He made the wheels come off their chariots, so that they could hardly drive. Then the Egyptians said, "We must run from Israel, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is fighting on their side against Egypt!"
en.R: He made the wheels of their chariots come off, so it was very hard for them to drive. The Egyptians shouted, "Run! Get away from the Israelites! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is fighting for them against Egypt!"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quitó las ruedas de sus carros y los hizo avanzar con pesadez. Y los egipcios dijeron: «Huyamos de delante de Israel, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} pelea por ellos contra Egipto».
es.B: Hizo que se soltaran las ruedas de sus carros, de modo que apenas podían avanzar. Entonces los egipcios dijeron: «¡Tenemos que huir de Israel, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} pelea a su favor contra Egipto!».
es.R: Hizo que las ruedas de sus carros se salieran, y les costaba mucho avanzar. Los egipcios gritaron: «¡{{plural_you:Corran|Corred}}! ¡Huyamos de los israelitas! ¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} pelea por ellos contra Egipto!».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ôta les roues de leurs chars, et les fit avancer avec lourdeur. Et les Égyptiens dirent : « Fuyons devant Israël, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} combat pour eux contre l’Égypte. »
fr.B: Il fit se détacher les roues de leurs chars, si bien qu’ils avançaient à grand-peine. Alors les Égyptiens dirent : « Il faut fuir devant Israël, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} combat pour eux contre l’Égypte ! »
fr.R: Il a fait sortir les roues de leurs chars, et ils avaient beaucoup de mal à avancer. Les Égyptiens ont crié : « Fuyez ! Éloignons-nous des Israélites ! {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} combat pour eux contre l’Égypte ! »

sw.L: Naye akayaondoa magurudumu ya magari yao, akayafanya yaende kwa uzito. Nao Wamisri wakasema, "Na tukimbie mbele ya Israeli, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anawapigania dhidi ya Misri."
sw.B: Aliyafanya magurudumu ya magari yao yang'oke, hata wakaendesha kwa shida sana. Kisha Wamisri wakasema, "Lazima tuwakimbie Waisraeli, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anapigana upande wao dhidi ya Misri!"
sw.R: Aliyafanya magurudumu ya magari yao yatoke, na ikawa vigumu sana kwao kuendesha. Wamisri wakapiga kelele, "Kimbieni! Tuwakimbie Waisraeli! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anawapigania dhidi ya Misri!"

decisions.choice: he removed: the Hebrew text
alternatives: he bound (clogged) the wheels of their chariots
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "he turned aside", that is, removed or jammed the wheels. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek translation have "he bound", a verb that differs by one letter in Hebrew: the wheels were clogged and stuck. Either way the chariots could not move freely. The translation follows the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: with heaviness: with difficulty, heavily
decisions.reason: "Heaviness" is from the same root as Pharaoh's "heavy" heart (7:14) and God's "getting glory" (verses 4, 17-18). The army that came out in strength now drags along heavily, and God is honored over it.

decisions.choice: Yahweh is fighting for them: the Egyptians say what Moses said
decisions.reason: Moses told Israel, "Yahweh will fight for you" (verse 14). Now the Egyptians themselves say it, and they begin to know that he is Yahweh (verses 4, 18).

decisions.choice: the Egyptians ... us / we
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "Egypt said, 'Let me flee'", the nation speaking as one person. Every level says "the Egyptians" and "us" or "we".
