source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה נְטֵ֥ה אֶת־יָדְךָ֖ עַל־הַיָּ֑ם וְיָשֻׁ֤בוּ הַמַּ֨יִם֙ עַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם עַל־רִכְבּ֖וֹ וְעַל־פָּרָשָֽׁיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, stretch out your hand over the sea, that may return the waters over Egypt, over his chariots and over his horsemen.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may return upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots and upon their horsemen."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Hold your hand out over the sea, and the waters will flow back over the Egyptians, over their chariots and their horsemen."
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Hold your hand out over the sea. The water will come back and cover the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «Extiende tu mano sobre el mar, para que las aguas vuelvan sobre los egipcios, sobre sus carros y sobre sus jinetes».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «Extiende tu mano sobre el mar, y las aguas volverán sobre los egipcios, sobre sus carros y sus jinetes».
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Extiende tu mano sobre el mar. El agua volverá y cubrirá a los egipcios y a sus carros y jinetes».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Étends ta main sur la mer, et que les eaux reviennent sur les Égyptiens, sur leurs chars et sur leurs cavaliers. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Tends la main au-dessus de la mer, et les eaux reviendront sur les Égyptiens, sur leurs chars et leurs cavaliers. »
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « Tends la main au-dessus de la mer. L’eau va revenir et recouvrir les Égyptiens, leurs chars et leurs cavaliers. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Nyosha mkono wako juu ya bahari, ili maji yarudi juu ya Wamisri, juu ya magari yao na juu ya wapanda farasi wao."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Nyosha mkono wako juu ya bahari, nayo maji yatarudi juu ya Wamisri, juu ya magari yao na wapanda farasi wao."
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Nyosha mkono wako juu ya bahari. Maji yatarudi na kuwafunika Wamisri pamoja na magari yao na wapanda farasi wao."

decisions.choice: stretch out your hand over the sea: the same act that opened the sea
decisions.reason: Moses opened the sea by stretching out his hand (verses 16, 21); the same act now closes it.

decisions.choice: that the waters may return: the result God intends
decisions.reason: The verb form states the purpose of the command and what will follow from it.

source.text: וַיֵּט֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה אֶת־יָד֜וֹ עַל־הַיָּ֗ם וַיָּ֨שָׁב הַיָּ֜ם לִפְנ֥וֹת בֹּ֨קֶר֙ לְאֵ֣יתָנ֔וֹ וּמִצְרַ֖יִם נָסִ֣ים לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וַיְנַעֵ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And stretched out Moses his hand over the sea, and returned the sea at [the] turning of morning to its usual flow, and Egypt [was] fleeing to meet it, and shook off Yahweh Egypt in [the] midst of the sea.

en.L: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned at the turning of morning to its usual flow, and the Egyptians [were] fleeing toward it, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shook off the Egyptians into the midst of the sea.
en.B: So Moses held his hand out over the sea, and as morning broke the sea went back to its usual flow. The Egyptians were fleeing straight into it, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shook them off into the middle of the sea.
en.R: So Moses held out his hand over the sea. As the sun came up, the water flowed back to where it belonged. The Egyptians tried to run away, but they ran right into the water. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} threw them into the middle of the sea.

es.L: Y extendió Moisés su mano sobre el mar, y el mar volvió al despuntar la mañana a su curso habitual, y los egipcios huían hacia él, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} sacudió a los egipcios en medio del mar.
es.B: Moisés extendió su mano sobre el mar, y al despuntar el día el mar volvió a su cauce. Los egipcios huían directamente hacia él, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los arrojó de una sacudida en medio del mar.
es.R: Moisés extendió su mano sobre el mar. Al salir el sol, el agua volvió a su lugar. Los egipcios trataron de escapar, pero corrieron justo hacia el agua. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los lanzó en medio del mar.

fr.L: Et Moïse étendit sa main sur la mer, et la mer revint, au tournant du matin, à son cours habituel ; et les Égyptiens fuyaient à sa rencontre, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} secoua les Égyptiens au milieu de la mer.
fr.B: Moïse tendit donc la main au-dessus de la mer, et au point du jour la mer reprit son cours habituel. Les Égyptiens s’enfuyaient droit vers elle, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les rejeta d’une secousse au milieu de la mer.
fr.R: Moïse a donc tendu la main au-dessus de la mer. Au lever du soleil, l’eau est revenue à sa place. Les Égyptiens ont essayé de s’enfuir, mais ils ont couru droit dans l’eau. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les a jetés au milieu de la mer.

sw.L: Naye Musa akaunyosha mkono wake juu ya bahari, nayo bahari ikarudi, kulipopambazuka, katika hali yake ya kawaida; nao Wamisri walikuwa wakikimbia kuielekea, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawakung'uta Wamisri katikati ya bahari.
sw.B: Basi Musa akaunyosha mkono wake juu ya bahari, na kulipopambazuka bahari ikarudi katika hali yake ya kawaida. Wamisri walikuwa wakikimbia moja kwa moja kuielekea, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawakung'utia katikati ya bahari.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Musa aliunyosha mkono wake juu ya bahari. Jua lilipochomoza, maji yalirudi mahali pake. Wamisri walijaribu kukimbia, lakini walikimbilia moja kwa moja majini. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatupa katikati ya bahari.

decisions.choice: its usual flow: its normal, steady state
decisions.reason: The word means what is constant or lasting, like a stream that always flows (Deuteronomy 21:4; Amos 5:24). The sea went back to the way it always was.

decisions.choice: shook off: threw off, as one shakes something off
decisions.reason: The verb is used of shaking something off or out (Judges 16:20; Nehemiah 5:13). Psalm 136:15 uses the same verb of this event: God shook off Pharaoh and his army in the sea.

decisions.choice: fleeing toward it: running into the returning water
decisions.reason: The Egyptians tried to escape (verse 25), but they ran toward the water as it came back.

decisions.choice: threw
decisions.reason: Readable says "threw" for the picture of shaking off.

source.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ הַמַּ֗יִם וַיְכַסּ֤וּ אֶת־הָרֶ֨כֶב֙ וְאֶת־הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים לְכֹל֙ חֵ֣יל פַּרְעֹ֔ה הַבָּאִ֥ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּיָּ֑ם לֹֽא־נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּהֶ֖ם עַד־אֶחָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned the waters and covered the chariots and the horsemen, [even] all [the] army of Pharaoh which had gone after them into the sea; not remained among them even one.

en.L: And the waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen, all the army of Pharaoh that had gone in after them into the sea; there did not remain among them even one.
en.B: The waters came back and covered the chariots and the horsemen, the whole of Pharaoh's army that had followed Israel into the sea. Not a single one of them was left.
en.R: The water came back and covered the chariots and the horsemen. It covered Pharaoh's whole army that had followed the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.

es.L: Y volvieron las aguas y cubrieron los carros y los jinetes, todo el ejército del faraón que había entrado tras ellos en el mar; no quedó de ellos ni uno.
es.B: Las aguas regresaron y cubrieron los carros y los jinetes, todo el ejército del faraón que había seguido a Israel dentro del mar. No quedó ni uno solo de ellos.
es.R: El agua volvió y cubrió los carros y los jinetes. Cubrió a todo el ejército del faraón que había seguido a los israelitas dentro del mar. No quedó vivo ni uno de ellos.

fr.L: Et les eaux revinrent et couvrirent les chars et les cavaliers, toute l’armée de Pharaon qui était entrée derrière eux dans la mer ; il n’en resta pas même un seul.
fr.B: Les eaux revinrent et recouvrirent les chars et les cavaliers, toute l’armée de Pharaon qui avait suivi Israël dans la mer. Il n’en resta pas un seul.
fr.R: L’eau est revenue et a recouvert les chars et les cavaliers. Elle a recouvert toute l’armée de Pharaon, qui avait suivi les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} dans la mer. Aucun d’eux n’est resté en vie.

sw.L: Nayo maji yakarudi, yakayafunika magari na wapanda farasi, jeshi lote la Farao lililoingia baharini nyuma yao; hakusalia hata mmoja wao.
sw.B: Maji yalirudi, yakayafunika magari na wapanda farasi, jeshi lote la Farao lililokuwa limewafuata Israeli baharini. Hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyebaki.
sw.R: Maji yalirudi, yakayafunika magari na wapanda farasi. Yalilifunika jeshi lote la Farao lililokuwa limewafuata Waisraeli baharini. Hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyebaki hai.

decisions.choice: all the army of Pharaoh: that is, the whole force that went in
decisions.reason: The phrase sums up the chariots and horsemen: all of Pharaoh's army that followed Israel into the sea.

decisions.choice: not even one remained: as with the flies and the locusts
decisions.reason: The same words were said of the flies (8:27) and the locusts that were swept into the sea (10:19). Now it is said of Pharaoh's army.

decisions.choice: Israel / the Israelites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "after them"; Balanced and Readable say who they were.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָלְכ֥וּ בַיַּבָּשָׁ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיָּ֑ם וְהַמַּ֤יִם לָהֶם֙ חֹמָ֔ה מִֽימִינָ֖ם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָֽם

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Israel walked on dry ground in [the] midst of the sea, and the waters [were] to them a wall on their right and on their left.

en.L: But the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea, and the waters [were] a wall to them on their right and on their left.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, though, walked on dry ground through the middle of the sea, with the water a wall for them to the right and to the left.
en.R: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground. The water was like a wall on their right and on their left.

es.L: Pero los hijos de Israel anduvieron sobre tierra seca por en medio del mar, y las aguas [eran] para ellos un muro a su derecha y a su izquierda.
es.B: Los israelitas, en cambio, caminaron sobre tierra seca por en medio del mar, con el agua como un muro a su derecha y a su izquierda.
es.R: Pero los israelitas caminaron por en medio del mar sobre tierra seca. El agua era como una pared a su derecha y a su izquierda.

fr.L: Mais les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël marchèrent sur la terre sèche au milieu de la mer, et les eaux [étaient] pour eux une muraille à leur droite et à leur gauche.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, eux, marchèrent à pied sec au milieu de la mer, l’eau formant pour eux une muraille à droite et à gauche.
fr.R: Mais les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont marché au milieu de la mer sur un sol sec. L’eau était comme un mur à leur droite et à leur gauche.

sw.L: Lakini wana wa Israeli walitembea juu ya nchi kavu katikati ya bahari, nayo maji [yalikuwa] ukuta kwao upande wao wa kulia na upande wao wa kushoto.
sw.B: Waisraeli, kwa upande wao, walitembea juu ya nchi kavu katikati ya bahari, maji yakiwa ukuta kwao kulia na kushoto.
sw.R: Lakini Waisraeli walitembea katikati ya bahari juu ya nchi kavu. Maji yalikuwa kama ukuta upande wa kulia na upande wa kushoto.

decisions.choice: but the sons of Israel walked: a contrast with the Egyptians
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with its subject, setting Israel against the drowned Egyptians of verse 28. It repeats verse 22 as a summary: those who went in after them died; Israel walked through.

source.text: וַיּ֨וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיַּ֤רְא יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵ֖ת עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And saved Yahweh on that day Israel from [the] hand of Egypt, and saw Israel Egypt dead on [the] shore of the sea.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved Israel on that day from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore of the sea.
en.B: So on that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved Israel from the power of Egypt, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead along the edge of the sea.
en.R: That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved Israel from the Egyptians. The Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians lying on the seashore.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} salvó a Israel en aquel día de la mano de los egipcios, e Israel vio a los egipcios muertos sobre la ribera del mar.
es.B: Así, aquel día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} salvó a Israel del poder de Egipto, e Israel vio a los egipcios muertos por toda la orilla del mar.
es.R: Ese día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} salvó a Israel de los egipcios. Los israelitas vieron los cuerpos de los egipcios tirados en la playa.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sauva Israël en ce jour-là de la main des Égyptiens, et Israël vit les Égyptiens morts sur le rivage de la mer.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sauva donc Israël du pouvoir de l’Égypte, et Israël vit les Égyptiens morts au bord de la mer.
fr.R: Ce jour-là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a sauvé Israël des Égyptiens. Les Israélites ont vu les corps des Égyptiens étendus sur le rivage.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawaokoa Israeli siku ile kutoka mkononi mwa Wamisri, nao Israeli wakawaona Wamisri wamekufa ufuoni mwa bahari.
sw.B: Hivyo siku hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaokoa Israeli kutoka katika nguvu za Misri, nao Israeli wakawaona Wamisri wakiwa wamekufa kando ya bahari.
sw.R: Siku hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaokoa Waisraeli kutoka kwa Wamisri. Waisraeli waliziona maiti za Wamisri zikiwa zimelala ufuoni mwa bahari.

decisions.choice: saved: rescued, delivered
decisions.reason: The verb is the root of "salvation" in verse 13. What Moses promised has happened.

decisions.choice: from the hand of the Egyptians: from their power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control (3:8; 18:9-10).

decisions.choice: Israel saw the Egyptians dead: Moses' word in verse 13 fulfilled
decisions.reason: Moses said they would never see the Egyptians again. They see them once more, but dead: the threat is over.

decisions.choice: from the power of Egypt (Balanced); from the Egyptians (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the hand" means; Literal keeps it.

source.text: וַיַּ֨רְא יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־הַיָּ֣ד הַגְּדֹלָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּֽירְא֥וּ הָעָ֖ם אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽאֲמִ֨ינוּ֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וּבְמֹשֶׁ֖ה עַבְדּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And saw Israel the hand the great which had done Yahweh against Egypt, and feared the people Yahweh, and they believed in Yahweh and in Moses his servant.

en.L: And Israel saw the great hand that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done against Egypt, and the people feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they believed in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and in Moses {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant.
en.B: Israel had seen the great hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at work against Egypt. So the people feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they believed in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and in Moses, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant.
en.R: When the Israelites saw what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done to Egypt with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power, they were filled with awe before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They believed in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and in Moses, who served {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y vio Israel la gran mano que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mostrado contra Egipto, y el pueblo temió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y creyeron en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y en Moisés, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} siervo.
es.B: Israel había visto la gran mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} actuando contra Egipto. Por eso el pueblo temió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y creyó en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y en Moisés, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} siervo.
es.R: Cuando los israelitas vieron lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había hecho a Egipto con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gran poder, se llenaron de reverencia ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Creyeron en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y en Moisés, que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servía.

fr.L: Et Israël vit la grande main que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait déployée contre l’Égypte, et le peuple craignit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et ils crurent en {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et en Moïse, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur.
fr.B: Israël avait vu la grande main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} à l’œuvre contre l’Égypte. Alors le peuple craignit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et il crut en {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et en Moïse, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur.
fr.R: Quand les Israélites ont vu ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait fait à l’Égypte par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grande puissance, ils ont été remplis de respect devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ils ont cru en {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et en Moïse, qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servait.

sw.L: Nao Israeli wakauona ule mkono mkuu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliuonyesha juu ya Wamisri, nao watu wakamcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakamwamini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na Musa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Israeli walikuwa wameuona mkono mkuu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukifanya kazi dhidi ya Misri. Kwa hiyo watu wakamcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakamwamini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na Musa, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Waisraeli walipoona yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatendea Wamisri kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kuu, walijawa na hofu ya heshima mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Walimwamini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na Musa, aliyemtumikia.

decisions.choice: the great hand: the great power and the mighty deed
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power, and here for what that power did. God had promised to bring Israel out with a strong hand (3:19-20; 6:1).

decisions.choice: feared Yahweh: stood in awe of him
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 10, where the people were afraid of the Egyptians. Now their fear is turned to Yahweh: reverence and awe at what he has done.

decisions.choice: they believed in Yahweh and in Moses his servant: the fear of 4:1 answered
decisions.reason: Moses feared the people would not believe him (4:1). They believed at the signs (4:31), lost heart under their labor (6:9), and now believe in Yahweh and in Moses. Moses is called Yahweh's servant again in Numbers 12:7 and Deuteronomy 34:5.

decisions.choice: the great hand of the LORD at work (Balanced); his great power (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the hand; Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: were filled with awe before
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "feared" here, which is reverence, not terror. Literal and Balanced keep "feared".
